payload.why_pivotal: Without consent, incurring any of the permitted offers would breach the senior secured Knight loan ($12.3M), and a default on third-party debt automatically defaults the Knight loan; this gates every offer regardless of cash coverage.
payload.acceptable_evidence: Signed Knight consent/waiver or the executed Knight loan agreement text showing a permitted-debt basket covering the advance; intercreditor terms.
payload.if_resolved: If consent exists: evaluate offers on cash coverage (settlement payments, reserve). If no consent: no offer can be supported; only a structure paid out with or subordinated under Knight's approval could be considered.

payload.fact: How much of the $2,000,000 2024 Atrium settlement-loan payments and the $600,000 2024 March 27, 2024 supplier-settlement payments had been paid between June 30 and August 13, 2024, and on what dates are the remaining installments due?
payload.why_pivotal: With about $2.0M reported cash, $100,000 restricted and a $200,000 illustrative reserve, the settlement buckets alone leave a $900,000 cumulative shortfall if nothing was paid, $250,000 if 25% was paid, and none if at least 50% was paid, before any new advance installments.
payload.acceptable_evidence: Settlement agreement payment schedules; bank records of payments to Atrium/HVL and the supplier after June 30, 2024; borrower-certified payables aging.
payload.if_resolved: If ≥50% was paid, the settlement requirement is covered by reported cash plus reserve and offer comparison turns on operating receipts; if little was paid, the 2024 settlement payments exceed available cash and even the $100k offer adds strain.

payload.summary: Synergy CHC Corp., as of Aug 13, 2024; $250k/6m request versus the $100k/6m and $250k/3m analytical offers. Atrium lawsuit settled Dec 2023 into a $5,450,000 loan payable (fnd_003). The Dec 28, 2023 settlement loan requires $2,000,000 in 2024 (fnd_019) and had a $4,802,445 balance at June 30, 2024 (fnd_007) — eff_005; its identity with Atrium is an inference (fnd_006). The $2,235,986 gain is a non-cash cost-of-sales reduction (eff_019). The March 27, 2024 supplier settlement loan requires $600,000 in 2024 (eff_006). LODC and Valenti are paid (eff_012). Knight covenant: 'Synergy shall not add any other debt without paying out KTI first', with automatic cross-default (eff_007). No 2024 Knight or Sanders principal. $100k restricted cash (eff_010). CEO-entity note: $1,716,496 received, $130,000 repaid (eff_015). Sensitivity: required net cash is $900,000 at 0% paid, $250,000 at 25%, $0 at ≥50%. Incomplete: the Jev check ceiling was reached and 18 inventory items were escalated.
pivotal_unknowns: Knight consent to additional debt without payout (fact_001)
Amount of the $2,000,000 Atrium and $600,000 supplier 2024 settlement payments paid after June 30, 2024 (fact_002)

Whether the ~$2.0M Aug 12 cash includes the $100,000 restricted collateral
payload.conclusion: No lending conclusion is reached, and the review is incomplete (Jev check quota exhausted; items escalated). Under the Knight loan, Synergy shall not add any other debt without paying out Knight first, and a default on any third-party debt automatically defaults the Knight loan. Whether Knight has consented to a new advance is therefore the pivotal missing fact. Synergy is required to pay $2,000,000 in 2024 on the Atrium settlement loan (the Atrium link is inferred from matching amounts and cross-references) and $600,000 in 2024 on the March 27, 2024 supplier settlement loan. With about $2.0M of reported cash, $100,000 unavailable and a $200,000 illustrative reserve, the sensitivity shows required net cash of $900,000 if none of these amounts was paid since measurement, $250,000 at 25% paid, and $0 at 50% or more. The $2,235,986 Atrium settlement gain reduced 2023 cost of sales and creates no cash inflow.
